summary: Detect NFC tags, read messages that contain NDEF data, and save data to writable tags.

declarations.name: CardSession
declarations.comment:
ISO7816 card emulation session.

This is the session to allow ISO7816-4 protocol communication, send and receive Application Protocol Data Units (APDUs), with a NFC reader.  To use this session:

1. Instantiate a new `CardSession` object.  This will start the `eventStream`; `.sessionStarted` will be posted when the session becomes active.
   Once the session is started `Event.readerDetected` event will be generated when an external NFC field is detected.
   Optionally you may call `startEmulation()` to immediately start the card emulation regardless if an NFC reader is present.
2. Wait for `Event.readerDetected` to detect the presence of an external NFC reader.
3. Call `startEmulation()` when you app is ready to handle APDUs sent by the reader.  This is when card emulation is enabled and reader can be connected to the device.
4. When `Event.received()` is received, process the APDU data, generate a response, and send it out using `APDU.respond(response:)`. If you don't send out the response,
   reader may detect a timeout conditions and generates error condition.
5.`Event.readerDeselected` is triggered when reader's field is turned off or device is pull away from the reader.
6. Call `invalidate()` to terminate the session.

At any time `stopEmulation(status:)` can be called to stop card emulation (after emulation has been started previously).  Note that stopping emulation at the wrong time can
cause RF tearing and triggers error on the reader.

NOTES:
- Session is valid up to 60 seconds starting from the first`startEmulation()` call.  Once this timeout occurs, `sessionInvalidated(reason: .maxSessionDurationReached)`
  will be returned from the event stream and the session will be invalidated.
- A modal UI with text controlled by `alertMessage` will be shown on top of your app after `startEmulation()` is called.  It will get dismissed when `stopEmulation(status:)` is called or session is invalidated.
- `systemNotAvailable` indicates system is currently unavailable to accept your request; this is a temporal condition and you may retry the operation in a later time.
- Special entitlement is required to use this service.  As part of this entitlement you are required to declare a list of ISO7816 application identifiers (AID) prefixes that your application will be listen on
  when receiving the SELECT command from the reader.  A `fatalError()` will occur on `CardSession.init()` if the necessary entitlement is missing.
- `isEligible` can be used to determined if system is eligible to use the card session before instantiation.
- `isSupported` shall be used to determine if the device supports NFC card session functionality.  `fatalError()` will get triggered when `CardSession.init()` is called on unsupported hardware.

members.name: alertMessage
members.comment:
Descriptive text message that is displayed on the alert action sheet once card emulation has started.  The string can be updated
dynamically in any thread context as long as the session is valid.  This should be set prior to calling `startEmulation()` to display
the correct message.  Use this string to provide additional context about the NFC card emulation process.

members.name: init
members.comment:
Request to start a card session. Successful session start depends on the following conditions:
- Device eligibility for using card session.
- User has accepted your app request to use card session.

Refer to `CardSession.Error` on possible errors.  `fatalError()` will get triggered if `isSupported` returns false.

members.name: respond
members.signature: final func respond(response: Data) async throws
members.comment:
The client must respond to each APDU.  Error is thrown if system fails to send.
- If the client disposes the `APDU` object without responding, it will end card emulation.
- `fatalError()` will get triggered if a) call more than once, 2) empty data is used.

members.name: sendFeliCaCommand
members.signature: @preconcurrency func sendFeliCaCommand(commandPacket: Data, resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<Data, any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Transmission of FeliCa Command Packet Data at the application layer. Refer to the FeliCa specification for details.
Manufacturer ID (IDm) of the currently selected system can be read from the currentIDm property.

- Parameters:
 - commandPacket:  Command packet send to the FeliCa card. Maximum packet length is 254. Data length (LEN) byte and CRC bytes are calculated and inserted
                   automatically to the provided packet data frame.
 - resultHandler:  Completion handler called when the operation is completed. A `NFCErrorDomain` error is returned when there is a communication issue with the tag.
members.typescript: sendFeliCaCommand(commandPacket: ArrayBuffer, resultHandler: ((arg0: SDKHandle) => void)): void

members.name: requestService
members.signature: @preconcurrency func requestService(nodeCodeList: [Data], resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<[Data], any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Request Service command defined by FeliCa card specification. Refer to the FeliCa specification for details.

- Parameters:
  - nodeCodeList:   Node Code list represented in an array of Data objects. Number of nodes specified should be between 1 to 32 inclusive.
                    Each node code should be 2 bytes stored in Little Endian format.
  - resultHandler:  Completion handler called when the operation is completed. Node key version list is returned as an array of Data objects,
                    and each data object is stored in Little Endian format per FeliCa specification.
members.typescript: requestService(nodeCodeList: Array<ArrayBuffer>, resultHandler: ((arg0: SDKHandle) => void)): void

members.comment:
Request Response command defined by FeliCa card specification. Refer to the FeliCa specification for details.

- Parameters:
  - resultHandler:  Returns the mode as Int or a `NFCErrorDomain` error when the operation is completed. Valid mode value ranges from 0 to 3 inclusively.

members.comment:
Request Service V2 command defined by FeliCa card specification.  Refer to the FeliCa specification for details.

- Parameters:
  - nodeCodeList:   Node Code list represent in an array of Data. Number of nodes specified should be between 1 to 32 inclusive. Each node code should be 2 bytes stored in Little Endian format.
  - resultHandler:  Completion handler called when the operation is completed. `encryptionIdentifier` value shall be ignored if Status Flag 1 value indicates an error.
                    `nodeKeyVersionListAES` and `nodeKeyVersionListDES` may be nil depending on the Status Flag 1 value and the Encryption Identifier value.
                    The 2 bytes node key version (AES and DES) is in Little Endian format.
members.typescript: requestServiceV2(nodeCodeList: Array<ArrayBuffer>, resultHandler: ((arg0: SDKHandle) => void)): void

members.name: readWithoutEncryption
members.signature: @preconcurrency func readWithoutEncryption(serviceCodeList: [Data], blockList: [Data], resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<(NFCFeliCaStatusFlag, [Data]), any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Read Without Encryption command defined by FeliCa card specification.  Refer to the FeliCa specification for details.

- Parameters:
  - serviceCodeList:    Service Code list represented in an array of Data objects. Number of nodes specified should be between 1 to 16 inclusive.
                        Each service code should be 2 bytes stored in Little Endian format.
  - blockList:          Block List represent in an array of Data objects. 2-Byte or 3-Byte block list element is supported.
  - resultHandler:      Completion handler called when the operation is completed. Valid read data blocks (block length of 16 bytes) are returned
                        in an array of Data objects when Status Flag 1 equals zero.
members.typescript: readWithoutEncryption(serviceCodeList: Array<ArrayBuffer>, blockList: Array<ArrayBuffer>, resultHandler: ((arg0: SDKHandle) => void)): void

members.name: writeWithoutEncryption
members.signature: @preconcurrency func writeWithoutEncryption(serviceCodeList: [Data], blockList: [Data], blockData: [Data], resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<NFCFeliCaStatusFlag, any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Write Without Encryption command defined by FeliCa card specification.  Refer to the FeliCa specification for details.

- Parameters:
  - serviceCodeList:    Service Code list represented in an array of Data objects. Number of nodes specified should be between 1 to 16 inclusive.
                        Each service code should be 2 bytes stored in Little Endian format.
  - blockList:          Block List represent in an array of Data objects. Total blockList items and blockData items should match. 2-Byte or 3-Byte block list element is supported.
  - blockData:          Block data represent in an array of Data objects. Total blockList items and blockData items should match. Data block should be 16 bytes in length.
  - resultHandler:      Returns `NFCFeliCaStatusFlag` or a `NFCErrorDomain` error when operation is completed.
members.typescript: writeWithoutEncryption(serviceCodeList: Array<ArrayBuffer>, blockList: Array<ArrayBuffer>, blockData: Array<ArrayBuffer>, resultHandler: ((arg0: SDKHandle) => void)): void

members.name: requestSpecificationVersion
members.comment:
Request Specification Version command defined by FeliCa card specification.  This command supports response format version `00`h. Refer to the FeliCa specification for details.

- Parameters:
  - resultHandler:  Returns `NFCFeliCaRequestSpecificationVersionResponse` or a `NFCErrorDomain` error when the operation is completed.
                    `basicVersion` and `optionVersion` may be nil depending on the Status Flag 1 value and if the tag supports AES/DES.

members.name: polling
members.signature: @preconcurrency func polling(systemCode: Data, requestCode: NFCFeliCaPollingRequestCode, timeSlot: NFCFeliCaPollingTimeSlot, resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<NFCFeliCaPollingResponse, any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Polling command defined by FeliCa card specification.  Refer to the FeliCa specification for details.
System code must be one of the provided values in the "com.apple.developer.nfc.readersession.felica.systemcodes" in the Info.plist;
`NFCReaderErrorSecurityViolation` will be returned when an invalid system code is used.  Polling with wildcard value in the upper or lower byte is not supported.

- Parameters:
  - systemCode:     Designation of System Code.  Wildcard value (0xFF) in the upper or the lower byte is not supported.
  - requestCode:    Designation of Requset Data output.
  - timeSlot:       Maximum number of slots possible to respond.
  - resultHandler:  Returns `NFCFeliCaPollingResponse` or a `NFCErrorDomain` error when the operation is completed.  Valid `requestData` is return when
                    `requestCode` is a non-zero parameter and feature is supported by the tag. The `currentIDM` property will be updated on each execution,
                    except when an invalid `systemCode` is provided and the existing selected system will stay selected.
members.typescript: polling(systemCode: ArrayBuffer, requestCode: NFCFeliCaPollingRequestCode, timeSlot: NFCFeliCaPollingTimeSlot, resultHandler: ((arg0: SDKHandle) => void)): void

members.name: readBuffer
members.signature: @preconcurrency func readBuffer(requestFlags flags: NFCISO15693RequestFlag, resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<(NFCISO15693ResponseFlag, Data), any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Read buffer command (0x3A command code) as defined in ISO15693-3 specification.

- Parameters:
  - flags:          Request flags.
  - resultHandler:  Completion handler called when the operation is completed. A `NFCErrorDomain` error is returned when there is a communication issue with the tag.
                    A NFCISO15693TagResponseErrorKey in NSError `userInfo` dictionary is returned when the tag responded to the command with an error,
                    and the error code value is defined in ISO15693-3 specification. Successfully command response will be return as Data object excluding the 8 bits response flag.

members.name: readBuffer
members.signature: func readBuffer(requestFlags flags: NFCISO15693RequestFlag) async throws -> (NFCISO15693ResponseFlag, Data)
members.comment:
Read buffer command (0x3A command code) as defined in ISO15693-3 specification.

- Parameters:
  - flags:          Request flags.
- Returns:
  A `(NFCISO15693ResponseFlag, Data)` tuple; data consists of Parameters and Data field per "Response Format" definition from the specification.
  A `NFCErrorDomain` error is returned when there is a communication issue with the tag.
  A NFCISO15693TagResponseErrorKey in NSError `userInfo` dictionary is returned when the tag responded to the command with an error,
  and the error code value is defined in ISO15693-3 specification.

members.name: systemInfo
members.signature: func systemInfo(requestFlags flags: NFCISO15693RequestFlag) async throws -> NFCISO15693SystemInfo
members.comment:
Get system information command (0x2B command code) as defined in ISO15693-3 specification. Address flag is automatically enforced by default and the
tag's UID is sent with the command; setting RequestFlagSelect to flags will disable the Address flag.

- Parameters:
  - flags:          Request flags.
- Returns:
  A `NFCISO15693SystemInfo` object.  A `NFCErrorDomain` error is returned when there is a communication issue with the tag.
  A `NFCISO15693TagResponseErrorKey` in NSError `userInfo` dictionary is returned when the tag responded to the command with an error,
  and the error code value is defined in ISO15693-3 specification.

members.name: sendRequest
members.signature: @preconcurrency func sendRequest(requestFlags flags: Int, commandCode: Int, data: Data?, resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<(NFCISO15693ResponseFlag, Data?), any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Send a command according to the ISO15693-3 specification. The request data frame is concatenation of 8 bits request flag, 8 bits command code, and optional data.
The 8 bits response flag and the data are returned in the completion handler.

- Parameters:
  - flags:          Request flags.
  - commandCode:    8 bis command code.
  - data:           Data follows after the command code.
  - resultHandler:  Returns a `(NFCISO15693ResponseFlag, Data)` tuple; data consists of Parameters and Data field per "Response Format" definition from the specification.

members.signature: @preconcurrency func authenticate(requestFlags flags: NFCISO15693RequestFlag, cryptoSuiteIdentifier: Int, message: Data, resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<(NFCISO15693ResponseFlag, Data), any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Authenticate command (0x35 command code) as defined in ISO15693-3 specification.  Please note that in-process reply is returned to the caller without any processing.

- Parameters:
  - flags:                  Request flags.
  - cryptoSuiteIdentifier:  8 bits Crypto Suite Indicator as defined in ISO/IEC 29167 specification.
  - message:                Content of the Authenticate command as dictated by the Crypto Suite Indicator.
  - resultHandler:          Completion handler called when the operation is completed. A `(NFCISO15693ResponseFlag, Data)` tuple is returned on success;
                            data consists of Parameters and Data field per "Response Format" definition from the specification.
                            A `NFCErrorDomain` error is returned when there is a communication issue with the tag.
                            A `NFCISO15693TagResponseErrorKey` in NSError `userInfo` dictionary is returned when the tag responded to the command with an error,
                            and the error code value is defined in ISO15693-3 specification.

members.comment:
Authenticate command (0x35 command code) as defined in ISO15693-3 specification.  Please note that in-process reply is returned to the caller without any processing.

- Returns:

  A `NFCErrorDomain` error is returned when there is a communication issue with the tag.
  A `NFCISO15693TagResponseErrorKey` in NSError `userInfo` dictionary is returned when the tag responded to the command with an error,

members.signature: @preconcurrency func customCommand(requestFlags flags: NFCISO15693RequestFlag, customCommandCode: Int, customRequestParameters: Data, resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<Data, any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Custom command (0xA0 to 0xDF command code) as defined in ISO15693-3 specification. IC manufacturer code from the tag is automatically inserted after the command byte
before appending the custom request parameters in forming the packet.

- Parameters:
  - flags:                      Request flags.
  - customCommandCode:          Custom command code defined by the IC manufacturer.  Valid range is 0xA0 to 0xDF inclusively.
  - customRequestParameters:    Custom request parameters defined by the command.
  - resultHandler:              Completion handler called when the operation is completed. A `NFCErrorDomain` error is returned when there is a communication issue with the tag.
                                A `NFCISO15693TagResponseErrorKey` in NSError `userInfo` dictionary is returned when the tag responded to the command with an error,
                                and the error code value is defined in ISO15693-3 specification. The custom response parameters are returned on success.
members.typescript: customCommand(flags: NFCISO15693RequestFlag, customCommandCode: number, customRequestParameters: ArrayBuffer, resultHandler: ((arg0: SDKHandle) => void)): void

members.signature: @preconcurrency func getSystemInfo(requestFlags flags: NFCISO15693RequestFlag, resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<NFCISO15693SystemInfo, any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Get system information command (0x2B command code) as defined in ISO15693-3 specification. Address flag is automatically enforced by default and the
tag's UID is sent with the command; setting RequestFlagSelect to flags will disable the Address flag.

- Parameters:
  - flags:          Request flags.
  - resultHandler:  Completion handler called when the operation is completed. A `NFCErrorDomain` error is returned when there is a communication issue with the tag.
                    A `NFCISO15693TagResponseErrorKey` in NSError `userInfo` dictionary is returned when the tag responded to the command with an error,
                    and the error code value is defined in ISO15693-3 specification. `blockSize` returns the actual block size in bytes ranged from 1 to 32.
                    `totalBlocks` returns the actual number of blocks ranged from 1 to 256 blocks.

members.name: readSingleBlock
members.signature: @preconcurrency func readSingleBlock(requestFlags flags: NFCISO15693RequestFlag, blockNumber: UInt8, resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<Data, any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Read single block command (0x20 command code) as defined in ISO15693-3 specification. Address flag is automatically
enforced by default and the tag's UID is sent with the command; setting RequestFlagSelect to flags will disable the Address flag.

- Parameters:
  - flags:          Request flags.
  - blockNumber:    Block number. Blocks are numbered from 0 to 255 inclusively.
  - resultHandler:  Completion handler called when the operation is completed. A `NFCErrorDomain` error is returned when there is a communication issue with the tag.
                    A `NFCISO15693TagResponseErrorKey` in NSError `userInfo` dictionary is returned when the tag  responded to the command with an error,
                    and the error code value is defined in ISO15693-3 specification. Successfully read data blocks will be returned from Data object.
                    If Option flag in the request flags is set, then first byte of data block will contain the associated block security status.

members.name: readMultipleBlocks
members.signature: @preconcurrency func readMultipleBlocks(requestFlags flags: NFCISO15693RequestFlag, blockRange: NSRange, resultHandler: @escaping @Sendable (Result<[Data], any Error>) -> Void)
members.comment:
Read multiple blocks command (0x23 command code) as defined in ISO15693-3 specification. Address flag is automatically
enforced by default and the tag's UID is sent with the command; setting RequestFlagSelect to flags will disable the Address flag.

- Parameters:
  - flags:          Request flags.
  - blockRange:     The range of blocks. Valid start index range is 0 to 255 inclusively. Valid length is 1 to 256 inclusively.
  - resultHandler:  Completion handler called when the operation is completed. A `NFCErrorDomain` error is returned when there is a communication issue with the tag.
                    A `NFCISO15693TagResponseErrorKey` in NSError `userInfo` dictionary is returned when the tag responded to the command with an error,
                    and the error code value is defined in ISO15693-3 specification. Successfully read data blocks will be returned from an array of Data object.
                    If Option flag in the request flags is set, then first byte of each returned data block will contain the associated block security status.
                    Each data block element would have identical size.
members.typescript: readMultipleBlocks(flags: NFCISO15693RequestFlag, blockRange: SDKHandle, resultHandler: ((arg0: SDKHandle) => void)): void

  returned from `NFCTagReaderSessionDelegate.tagReaderSession(_:didInvalidateWithError:)` if the required entitlement is missing when session is started.

  "com.apple.developer.nfc.readersession.iso7816.select-identifiers" in the specified array order.  The tag is
  returned from the `NFCTagReaderSessionDelegate.tagReaderSession(_:didDetect:)` call on the first successful SELECT command.
  The `NFCISO7816Tag.initialSelectedAID` property returns the application identifier of the selected application.  Tag will not be returned
  to the `NFCTagReaderSessionDelegate` if no application described in "com.apple.developer.nfc.readersession.iso7816.select-identifiers" is found.
